title: Little Red Riding Hood
retold: A gentle retelling of the traditional tale (Perrault, 1697; Brothers Grimm, 1812) for children aged 4 to 6. Nobody is eaten: Grandma hides, and the woodcutter chases the wolf away.

text: Once upon a time, a little girl lived near a big green forest.
She wore a red cape with a hood, so everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood.
One morning, her mother filled a basket with bread and apples.
"Please take this to Grandma. Stay on the path!" said Mother.
Little Red skipped along the forest path.
Birds sang, and flowers grew all around.
Soon, she met a wolf.
"Where are you going, little girl?" asked the wolf.
"To Grandma's house," said Little Red.
"Pick some flowers for Grandma," said the wolf.
Little Red stopped to pick flowers, and the wolf ran ahead.
The wolf knocked on Grandma's door.
Grandma peeked out, saw the wolf, and hid in the closet.
The wolf put on Grandma's nightcap and jumped into her bed.
Little Red came in with her flowers.
"Grandma, what big ears you have!"
"All the better to hear you with!"
"Grandma, what big teeth you have!"
"That is not Grandma!" said Little Red.
"Help!"
A kind woodcutter heard her call.
He ran in, and the wolf ran far, far away.
Grandma came out of the closet, and they all shared bread and apples.
"I will always stay on the path," said Little Red.
The End.
